image_description: A close-up view of a grey whale surfacing in blue-green water. The image captures the dorsal side of the whale, showing its mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches and a series of dorsal knuckles (humps) along the back where a dorsal fin would typically be. The head is partially visible on the left, and the body extends towards the right, fading into the water. A distant shoreline is visible in the background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is partially submerged and angled away; the top of the rostrum and blowholes are not clearly visible due to the viewing angle and water obstruction.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly exhibits the characteristic mottled grey pattern with distinct white/light-grey patches consistent with barnacle infestations.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is no dorsal fin. Instead, a series of small humps (knuckles) are clearly visible running along the ridge of the back, which is a definitive trait of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body appears thick and robust, consistent with the massive scale of a baleen whale, though the full length is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the body skin shows the correct texture and coloration patterns.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and underwater; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external dorsal view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are located on the underside/lateral sides of the whale and are completely submerged/occluded in this dorsal surface view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are at the posterior end of the animal, which is either out of frame or deeply submerged and not visible in this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution texture of the skin shows roughness and raised areas (callosities/barnacles), matching the biological description.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness/blurring at the immediate contact line between the whale's skin and the water surface. While some blur is expected due to motion/water refraction, the edge lacks the crisp displacement one might expect from a heavy solid object breaking the surface tension, suggesting minor generative smoothing.

The background shoreline is extremely blurry and lacks detailed structure, appearing somewhat 'painted on'. This is likely a depth-of-field effect, but the lack of any coherent geometric features makes it slightly suspicious of AI background generation.
